claims.text: High configurational entropy suppresses phase separation in nanoalloys at high temperatures.
High configurational entropy suppresses oxidation in nanoalloys at high temperatures.
High configurational entropy promotes lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion produces sluggish atomic diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion helps maintain the structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys.
Multi-element random mixing produces local lattice distortions.
High configurational entropy increases mixing stability.
Distortion-hindered diffusion reduces elemental segregation and phase separation at high temperatures.
Distortion-hindered diffusion reduces oxidation at high temperatures.
After oxidative treatment near 800°C, the high-entropy nanoalloy will show less phase separation than a lower-entropy binary or simpler alloy.
After oxidative treatment near 800°C, the high-entropy nanoalloy will show less oxidation than a lower-entropy binary or simpler alloy.
The proposed stability advantage applies approximately from 700°C to 1000°C.
Within the stated temperature range, thermal energy activates diffusion while lattice distortion continues to slow it.
Above the stated temperature range or under substantially different atmospheres, the predicted stability advantage may disappear.

contradictions.description: The proposed control is described as a binary or ternary alloy with an identical nominal overall composition to a multi-principal-element high-entropy alloy. A binary or ternary alloy cannot retain an identical full elemental composition while also containing fewer constituent elements. The baseline is elsewhere described only as having a similar composition, creating an inconsistent and potentially composition-confounded comparison.
